text:
Irene Choi: Kicking off a quick sync here on default subnet tiering + NAT strategy for the Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha). Need to lock defaults this week so Vivek can stamp the alpha gate. Questions:
1) Do we ship 2-tier (public/private) or 3-tier (public/private/isolated)?
2) NAT default: single NAT GW vs per-AZ?
We can expose knobs, but want “secure/supportable by default” and not explode support matrix.

Victor Alvarez: For tiering: I strongly prefer 3-tier even if customers don’t use all tiers day 1.
- public: IGW + optional NAT
- private: egress via NAT (if enabled)
- isolated: no direct internet route (intended for data plane nodes if customer is strict)
It maps cleanly to common enterprise patterns and gives us a place to put things when customer says “no outbound”.

Nina Petrova: +1 to 3-tier. From perf/latency POV, NAT is also a choke point. If a customer is high throughput on image pulls/telemetry during install, single NAT in us-east-1a will be sad.
But I get the cost pushback.

Bruno Silva: From PS side: most pilots ask “give me minimal thing that works” and then later harden. If our default uses per-AZ NAT and costs them $$$ before they even get to first token, we’ll get yelled at.
Can we do default single NAT + option per-AZ, with doc that per-AZ is recommended for prod?

Allison Grant: My only ask: whatever tiering, please don’t create a situation where flow logs / CW logs can’t reach the sink without public egress. If NAT disabled + endpoints missing, install fails and we get noisy tickets.
If we do “isolated”, we need explicit guidance: use VPC endpoints for logs/ECR/S3 or expect failure.

Ethan Park: Installer assumptions:
- Control plane components (in VPC mode) expect subnets they can reach ECR/S3 from.
- If customer chooses “no public egress”, they *must* have endpoints + DNS resolution.
We can tolerate NAT disabled but then the preflight checks need to be strict + actionable.
Outputs wise we need stable: `private_subnet_ids`, `isolated_subnet_ids` (optional?), and `public_subnet_ids`.

Irene Choi: Ok, so leaning:
- Default topology = 3-tier (public/private/isolated)
- Default placement for “compute” subnets for Private = private tier (not isolated) unless customer explicitly opts into “private-only endpoints / no egress” profile.
- Expose isolated subnets for customers who want it.
NAT decision still open.

Victor Alvarez: NAT: I recommend default per-AZ NAT *if* we’re claiming “opinionated secure baseline.” Single NAT is a single-AZ blast radius and also cross-AZ traffic charges. In steady state, the $ difference is smaller than people think once you count data processing.
But alpha is about reference module usability, so I’m ok with default single NAT if docs are very clear.

Nina Petrova: We should be careful with calling it “secure” if default is single NAT. It’s not insecure per se, just lower availability. But customers conflate.
Maybe language in README: “Default NAT mode: single (cost-optimized). Recommended for production: per-AZ (availability-optimized).”

Marcus Lin: Security POV: NAT strategy isn’t a direct security issue, but supportability is. If single NAT causes weird intermittent install failures (timeouts pulling from ECR, etc), it becomes a security escalation because people ask to open internet egress broadly.
So I want us to strongly support the “private-only endpoints” path and make it easy.

Bruno Silva: Realistically: customers that can afford per-AZ NAT also ask for “no public egress” anyway. If they are locked down, NAT is off and endpoints are on.
The mid customers are the ones who do NAT and want cheapest.

Allison Grant: +1. If we have good endpoint defaults (ECR api + dkr, S3 gateway, CloudWatch Logs), then “NAT off” is viable. The module can be secure-by-default by creating endpoints when NAT is disabled.

Sahana Iyer: CI angle: integration tests will be more reliable if we keep the default path simple. A 3-tier VPC with optional NAT modes is fine, but we should keep the default example to one mode.
If we support both, we should run at least plan/apply for both modes in CI matrix (but that doubles cost/time). :grimacing:

Irene Choi: Re CI: we already planned a small matrix (region + NAT mode). I’m okay with 2x if we cap runs and do scheduled full applies.

Victor Alvarez: Proposal:
- Tiering default: 3-tier.
- NAT mode var: `nat_mode = "single" | "per_az" | "none"`
- Default `nat_mode = "single"`
- If `nat_mode = "none"`, we strongly encourage endpoint module enabled and validate required endpoints selected.
- Provide two examples:
  1) minimal: `single NAT` + endpoints (optional but recommended)
  2) locked-down: `no NAT` + required endpoints + private DNS

Nina Petrova: Works. But we need to be explicit which subnets are used by which components. Otherwise people dump everything into isolated and wonder why they can’t pull images.
Maybe in docs: “Installer nodes must be in private (egress) or isolated (endpoints) subnets.”

Ethan Park: +1 and we can encode in installer docs too.
Also: please don’t make NAT required for the module to work. Some customers literally cannot create IGW/NAT.

Irene Choi: Agreed.

Bruno Silva: One nuance: some enterprise accounts have existing centralized egress via TGW to a shared NAT/proxy VPC. For alpha, can we at least not block them?
E.g., allow route table override for private subnets (or accept “existing VPC” mode). But avoid footguns.

Victor Alvarez: Yeah, but I don’t want to open generic “arbitrary routes” in v1. It’ll blow up. Maybe we document as “non-goal for alpha” but keep an escape hatch:
- allow providing existing NAT GW ids? (hard)
- or just allow NAT disabled and let them route 0.0.0.0/0 to TGW themselves after apply.

Marcus Lin: If we leave escape hatch as “edit route tables yourself”, that’s an audit headache. But for alpha we can say unsupported. Ideally a controlled input like `private_egress_target = nat|tgw|none` with validation.

Irene Choi: Let’s keep alpha defaults narrow and explicitly document “centralized egress via TGW/proxy” as not supported by the reference modules *yet* (tracked separately). We can add a follow-up issue.

Allison Grant: Please make sure the default tagging includes cost center so Finance can see NAT spend per environment. If we ship per-AZ as recommended, customers will ask.

Sahana Iyer: Also tflint/checkov will complain if flow logs aren’t enabled or retention not set. For default modules, we should at least provide an obvious toggle with recommended defaults. (not strictly NAT, but ties to “baseline”).

Irene Choi: Ok.
Next step: I’ll update ADR draft with:
- 3-tier default
- NAT default single, options per-AZ/none
- language guidance (cost-optimized vs availability-optimized)
- explicit “no public egress” supported via endpoints + private DNS
Draft ADR here: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/ADR-0127+AWS+VPC+topology+for+Private+alpha (WIP)

Victor Alvarez: I’ll add a section on trade-offs + cross-AZ cost note (single NAT -> more cross-AZ traffic).

Nina Petrova: I’ll sanity check subnet sizing assumptions (we’ve had folks pick /28 and then get stuck). Please include validation that subnets are >= /24 for default example. Or at least warn.

Ethan Park: From installer side: if you can output a simple map like `subnet_tier_by_id` that would be gold, but not required for alpha.
At minimum: consistent output names and docs.

Bruno Silva: Can we also put a short “what should go where” diagram in the README? Even ASCII.

Allison Grant: +1 diagram and a note: if `nat_mode=none`, you must enable endpoints for ECR + S3 + logs or disable those integrations. Otherwise you’ll hit preflight errors.

Marcus Lin: Please add security callout: “NAT does not equal security boundary.” We should still keep SGs restrictive and not rely on outbound allow-all.

Irene Choi: Yep.
Action items:
- Irene: update ADR-0127 + ping for review EOD tomorrow
- Victor: add NAT tradeoff + cost notes
- Nina: subnet sizing + tier mapping feedback
- Ethan: confirm minimum outputs needed by installer
- Allison: logging/flow logs default recommendation language

Victor Alvarez: :thumbsup:

Nina Petrova: :thumbsup:

Ethan Park: :thumbsup:

Sahana Iyer: FYI if NAT modes are in CI matrix, I’ll need the vars to be deterministic (no random AZ ordering). We’ve had flaky diffs when AZ list changes.

Irene Choi: Good catch. We’ll pin AZ selection via `availability_zones` input in examples and in tests.

Bruno Silva: Thanks all. This will reduce PS time a lot if defaults are predictable.

Marcus Lin: +1. Please tag me when ADR is ready; security sign-off depends on the “no egress” story being solid.

Irene Choi: Will do.
